To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
poly(butylene succinates) reinforced with short sisals fibres are a viable alternative to conventional plastics for the manufacture of biocomposite products.

the mechanical properties of poly(butylene succinates) can be significantly improved through incorporation of short sisal fibres, but that the optimum fibre content and fibre length are strongly dependent on the type of mechanical properties to be improved.
the mechanical properties of poly(butylene succinates) composites reinforced by short sisal fibre are strongly dependent on the fibre length and the fibre content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of composites based on poly(butylene succinates) reinforced with short sisalfibres.

the development and characterisation of a biodegradable composite material based on poly(butylene succinat) reinforced with sisal fibres, which can be used as a substitute for conventional thermoplastic composites.
the preparation of poly(butylene succiniate)/sisal fibre composites with enhanced mechanical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanical properties of PBS composites reinforced with sisal fibres are influenced by the fibre content and the fibre length.
the mechanical properties of poly(butylene succinates) reinforced with short sisals are significantly improved.

the tensile and bending properties of the com-posites were enhanced by short sisal fibre reinforcement and that the surface treatment of sisal fibres with maleic anhydride was effective in improving the interfacial bonding between the matrix and the fibre.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical properties of composites reinforced with natural fibres are strongly influenced by the surface treatment and fibre length of the natural fibrous filler.
the tensile and impact properties of poly(butylene succinat) (PBS) composites reinforced by sisal fibres are significantly improved by the surface treatment of fibres and the fibre length.
the mechanical properties of poly(butylene succiniate) composites reinforced by sisal fibres can be significantly improved by the use of a proper fibre length and fibre content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composites with 10 wt% of sisal fibre showed a good balance between mechanical properties and processability.
the mechanical properties of PBS composites reinforced with sisal fibres were enhanced by the addition of short fibres.
poly(butylene succinite) composites reinforced by short sisal fibre have potential for use in engineering applications.
